answer.answer: Audit-ready reconciliation completed and persisted as checkpoint:019fa49e-b353-7562-a5f5-aaa3d9a7a499. No second canonical game-data snapshot was created.

claims.value: The lossless import star-rupture-game-analysis__20260708T190137Z preserves the original 21,674,717-byte ZIP (SHA-256 1a1c1ef0ae00905ced37f1221ab22c4b9268f2ebe17b7516e6c9cac67d7f6fa3) and verified extracted tree under ignored raw/. All 123 archive entries, comprising 115 manifested files plus CHECKSUMS.sha256, passed unzip and packaged SHA-256 verification. MANIFEST.csv and CHECKSUMS.sha256 remain tracked for auditability; the retained raw material includes duplicate third-party data, personalized save context, generated binaries, and legacy SQLite data.

The archive’s repeated build 23761620 claim is corrected to a two-axis boundary: its source/game data is Update 1 internal version 35118973, dated 2026-04-09 and contextually mapped to Steam build 22674441; the canonical capture is SRDB 2.3.4, snapshot ea-u1-gv35118973__srdb-2.3.4__20260711T050230Z, captured 2026-07-11. Hotfix 0.2.8 / Steam build 23761620 was only the latest public executable observed, not proven provenance for every numeric value. Archive reports remain legacy calculations until rerun against the canonical snapshot.

No competing game-data snapshot was created. The canonical corpus already covered all 468 items, 191 public buildings, 234 recipe definitions, 6 corporations, 77 Corporation levels, 121 export offers, 15 development upgrades, 3,259 map markers, and 3,094 loot entries. Selective promotion was limited to the player-save baseline, six Ore Excavator v2 recipe/producer associations, explicit consumable-effect assumptions, nine player-specific site/geography assets, and consolidated player-save, architecture, geography, progression, exploration, food, and remote-resource notes. Reconciliation also corrected the airlock item/building collision and normalized Training Corporation’s literal $undefined sentinel to null.

The complete 18-file Flowworks Campaign Sizing - Levels 8 to 15 family is rejected, superseded audit history under raw/ and must not become current guidance. The authoritative player-state model marks Flowworks site_selected_not_built and its staged plan planned_not_installed; whether construction began and Titanium node purity remain unknown. The current level-10 output plan contains one Stabilizer, one Nozzle, one Impeller, two Valves, one Turbine, and two Pumps; the second Stabilizer is deferred until before Scanner, and one HRS v2 is permitted only if recovery testing justifies it. The active RuptureOps pipeline, database, and canonical snapshot remain authoritative over the archived SQLite database, source JSON, delivery CSVs, workbook, scripts, and legacy reports.

answer.answer: Durable Geo Scanner guidance reconstructed and checkpointed as checkpoint:019fa49e-9c5b-7f51-b40f-6ed1521a1608.

claims.value: The first Geo Scanner activation produced two deaths before success. After the first death, the player respawned at a nearby claimed base, but it lacked replacement weapons and materials, forcing a walk back to Landerworks. On the second attempt, the temporary fire base had physically installed but unpowered turrets, so they provided no defense; the player was overwhelmed, corruption disabled the base and its claimed Regeneration Chamber, and the next respawn occurred at the starting launcher.

The successful intervention was a fully built-out temporary fire base with every turret powered. Their continuous automated engagement—the turrets “singing” against the wave—completed the scanner defense and turned the frustrating experience into a strongly positive one.

This chain is direct player field observation from one Update 1 encounter: unpowered turrets did nothing, and corruption coincided with the contested base and claimed Regeneration Chamber going offline. It does not establish a universal corruption threshold, complete Regeneration Chamber availability formula, or general disable rule.

For future activations, treat the scanner as a deliberate defense event: claim a nearby Regeneration Chamber but assume it may fail with the contested base; power every turret and verify tracking/firing before activation; keep replacement weapons, ammunition, healing, and rebuilding materials in a separate safe cache outside the corruption failure domain; and retain a route to a stable production base or launcher. Do not report Cargo service as installed—the first scanner base had none confirmed. The completed site appeared to provide two unusually good food-related rewards or stacks, possibly involving quantity 20, but the dictated report was ambiguous, so exact item names and counts remain unresolved.
source_paths: Topics/StarRupture/Player save - sites and freight network.md

answer.answer: Mission Timeline was selected, but the frozen implementation remained in progress. Source files and resources existed; simulator, tests, signing, and installation readiness were not verified.

claims.value: Mission Timeline is the selected visual source of truth. The requested acceptance gate was to implement its native Watch Session, run automated tests, exercise it in an iPhone simulator, and hand it back only when genuinely ready for phone installation.

At the frozen 2026-07-11 23:14 UTC cutoff, dirty `main` contained unrelated work and the new iOS work was isolated under untracked `ios/`. Present artifacts were `ios/project.yml`; generators `generate_app_icon.swift` and `generate_audio.swift`; `AppDelegate.swift`; domain files `AlertPlanner.swift`, `RuptureCycle.swift`, `RuptureCycleDefinitions.swift`, and `WatchSession.swift`; services `ForegroundFeedbackController.swift`, `NotificationService.swift`, and `ScreenAwakeController.swift`; three unit-test files and `RuptureOpsUITests.swift`; an original app icon, versioned phase-color assets, and four original warning sounds. XcodeGen was invoked at 2026-07-11 23:11 UTC. This was implementation scaffolding and partial code/resources, not verified completion.

No Swift file with an `@main` application entry and no SwiftUI Mission Timeline view were present. No successful `xcodebuild`, unit tests, UI tests, simulator launch, screenshot, visual QA, interaction verification, device signing, or phone-install handoff was recorded. Therefore simulator and install readiness remain unmet and must not be claimed.

Treat the cutoff as historical evidence rather than current repository truth. Continue by inspecting live repository and Git state, preserving unrelated dirty work, completing the `@main` and SwiftUI Mission Timeline entry path, generating or refreshing the Xcode project, building and running unit/UI tests, then performing simulator visual and interaction verification. Address signing and phone-install handoff only after those gates pass.

answer.answer: RuptureOps can publicly release only independently authored app code and original assets after provenance and build verification. Its current data corpus and personalized artifacts cannot be distributed.

claims.value: The third-party source permits crawling but publishes no explicit data/content reuse license. Its mirrored raw archive, normalized corpus, derived SQLite database, legacy snapshot/workbook, and other source-derived data remain private research assets; crawling permission is not redistribution permission.

Keep private the personalized imports: save state, player screenshots, three prompt-history dumps, conversation-derived decisions, play-history/save models, attachment provenance, and the imported package’s duplicate third-party corpus. Only manifests and promoted, provenance-labeled facts belong in version control; that allowance does not itself authorize public distribution.

Public-build candidates are independently authored implementation and original assets: the recorded iOS domain/services/tests, original app icon, versioned phase-color assets, and four original warning sounds. Do not publish copies embedded in the private benchmark fixture or its binary site/player images. At 2026-07-11 23:14 UTC the app was only implementation-in-progress: it lacked an `@main` entry, Mission Timeline view, successful build/tests, simulator QA, signing, and installation handoff. Therefore no install-ready public build is established by this evidence; live-repository inspection, provenance review, completion, and verification are required first.

The safe path is to separate independently authored app code and original assets from all private corpus/import directories, inspect current repository state, complete and verify the entry/UI/build/test/simulator/signing path, and audit asset provenance. Before distributing any third-party-derived facts or content, obtain explicit reuse permission from the source owner or replace the corpus with a separately licensed-data strategy and document that license. Until then, keep the repository and normalized corpus private and do not push the corpus to a public remote.
